hero.eyebrow: Analytics skills · No software to install
hero.title: Statistics for Analysts: learn by doing
hero.subtitle: Describe data, measure spread, read distributions, work with probability, build confidence intervals and test relationships in a working spreadsheet. Every calculation is checked.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can summarise a data set, quantify uncertainty and judge whether a link is worth believing.

outcomes.title: Describe data
outcomes.text: Mean, median, mode, percentiles and the right choice for each.

outcomes.title: Measure spread
outcomes.text: Range, IQR, variance, standard deviation and z-scores.

outcomes.title: Read shapes
outcomes.text: Frequency tables, histograms, the normal curve and skew.

outcomes.title: Work with chance
outcomes.text: Probability rules, conditional probability and expected value.

outcomes.title: Estimate honestly
outcomes.text: Samples, bias, standard error and confidence intervals.

outcomes.title: Test relationships
outcomes.text: Correlation, a line of best fit and what a p-value really means.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: every number is checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the survey project and the final assessment.

faq.q: Do I need to know advanced maths?
faq.a: No. You need arithmetic and the willingness to read a formula. Every formula is built step by step.
A spreadsheet in your browser. The same formulas work in Excel and Google Sheets.

faq.q: Is this enough to be a data analyst?
faq.a: It is the statistical core. Analysts also need data cleaning, a query language and visualisation, which are covered in other GrowQR courses.

activities.title: Mean, median and the outlier
activities.objective: Calculate the mean and median of a list and see how one extreme value pulls them apart.
activities.scenario: Eight people in a small firm earn (in thousands of rupees a month) the salaries below. One is the owner.
steps: In B11 find the mean with AVERAGE.
In B12 find the median with MEDIAN.
In B13 find the largest value with MAX.
In B14 work out the mean minus the median.

checks.label: B11 is the mean
checks.explain: The mean adds everything and divides by the count.

checks.label: B12 is the median
checks.explain: The median is the middle value when the numbers are in order.

checks.label: B13 is the highest salary
checks.explain: MAX finds the extreme value that is pulling the mean up.

checks.label: B14 is mean minus median
checks.explain: A big gap between mean and median warns of skewed data.

activities.title: Variance and standard deviation by hand
activities.objective: Build variance and standard deviation step by step, then confirm with the built-in functions.
activities.scenario: Six daily temperature readings are in B2:B7. Work out how spread out they are.
steps: In B9 find the mean.
In C2:C7 work out each deviation: the value minus the mean (use $B$9).
In D2:D7 square each deviation.
In B10 add the squares. In B11 divide by the count minus one to get the sample variance.
In B12 use STDEV and in B13 find the range (largest minus smallest).

checks.label: B9 is the mean
checks.explain: Deviations are measured from the mean.

checks.label: C2 is the first deviation
checks.explain: A deviation says how far a value is from the mean.

checks.label: C7 is the last deviation
checks.explain: Every row needs its own deviation.

checks.label: D7 is the squared deviation
checks.explain: Squaring removes minus signs so deviations cannot cancel.

checks.label: B10 adds the squares
checks.explain: The sum of squares measures total variation.

checks.label: B11 is the sample variance
checks.explain: For a sample we divide by n minus one, not n.

checks.label: B12 is the standard deviation
checks.explain: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, back in the original units.

checks.label: B13 is the range
checks.explain: The range is the gap between the largest and smallest values.

activities.title: Standardise scores with z-scores
activities.objective: Convert raw scores to z-scores so different tests can be compared.
activities.scenario: Five students took a test. Find each student's z-score: how many standard deviations above or below the mean they are.
steps: In B8 find the mean and in B9 the standard deviation (STDEV).
In C2 write a formula for the first z-score: (score minus mean) divided by standard deviation, with the mean and SD locked.
Write the other four z-scores.

checks.label: B8 is the mean
checks.explain: The mean of the scores is the centre.

checks.label: B9 is the standard deviation
checks.explain: The standard deviation is the typical distance from the mean.

checks.label: C2 is Anu's z-score
checks.explain: A z-score is (value minus mean) divided by standard deviation.

checks.label: C5 is Dev's z-score
checks.explain: Dev scored above the mean, so the z-score is positive.

checks.label: C4 is zero (Chitra scored the mean)
checks.hint: Chitra's score equals the mean, so her z-score is 0.
checks.explain: A z-score of 0 means exactly average.

activities.title: Build a frequency table and histogram
activities.objective: Count values into bins with COUNTIF and show the shape with a chart.
activities.scenario: Twenty students' marks are in B2:B21. Group them into ten-mark bins and chart the result.
steps: Bins are labelled in D2:D7. In E2 count marks below 50.
For each other bin subtract two COUNTIFs: for 60 to 69, count marks of 60 or more, minus marks of 70 or more.
Fill all six bins; the counts must add up to 20.
Add a bar chart with the bin labels as labels and the counts as values.

checks.label: E2 counts marks below 50
checks.explain: COUNTIF counts the values that meet one condition.

checks.label: E4 counts marks from 60 to 69
checks.explain: Subtract the count above the band from the count at or above its start.

checks.label: E5 counts marks from 70 to 79
checks.hint: Use the same pattern with 70 and 80.
checks.explain: Each band uses two COUNTIFs.

checks.label: E7 counts marks from 90 to 99
checks.explain: The top band needs only one COUNTIF.

checks.label: E8 totals 20 students
checks.explain: Every student must fall in exactly one band.

checks.label: A bar chart of the bands
checks.hint: Chart type bar, labels D2:D7, values E2:E7.
checks.explain: A histogram shows the shape of the data at a glance.

activities.title: Expected value of a game
activities.objective: Combine outcomes and probabilities into an expected value.
activities.scenario: A school fair game costs 10 rupees to play. The prize (after paying 10) and the chance of each outcome are in the table.
steps: In D2:D5 multiply each outcome's value by its probability.
In C6 check the probabilities add to 1.
In D6 add the products to get the expected value.
In B8 use IF to show Good for the player if the expected value is positive, otherwise Poor.

checks.label: D2 is the first product
checks.explain: Each outcome contributes its value times its chance.

checks.label: D5 is the jackpot product
checks.explain: A rare big prize still adds to the total.

checks.label: C6 shows the probabilities add to 1
checks.explain: Probabilities of all outcomes must add to 1.

checks.label: D6 is the expected value
checks.explain: Expected value is the long-run average gain per play.

checks.label: B8 says Good because the expected value is positive
checks.explain: A positive expected value means players win on average (an unusual fair-game result).

activities.title: A confidence interval for a mean
activities.objective: Turn a sample into a range that probably contains the true mean.
activities.scenario: A survey of 36 students found they sleep 52 hours... wait, weekly study time: mean 52 minutes a day, standard deviation 12. Give a 95% confidence interval for the true mean.
steps: In B5 work out the standard error: standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.
In B6 work out the margin of error: 1.96 times the standard error.
In B7 and B8 find the lower and upper limits of the interval.
In B9 show the interval width (upper minus lower).

checks.label: B5 is the standard error
checks.explain: The standard error shrinks as the sample grows.

checks.label: B6 is the margin of error
checks.explain: 1.96 standard errors covers 95% of a normal distribution.

checks.label: B7 is the lower limit
checks.explain: The interval is the mean minus and plus the margin.

checks.label: B8 is the upper limit
checks.explain: Upper limit: the mean plus the margin.

checks.label: B9 is the width
checks.explain: A narrower interval means a more precise estimate.

activities.title: Correlation and a line of best fit
activities.objective: Measure how two variables move together and predict one from the other.
activities.scenario: Eight students recorded hours of revision per week and their exam marks. Find how strongly they are related and predict a mark.
steps: In B11 find the correlation of hours (B2:B9) and marks (C2:C9) with CORREL.
In B12 find the slope of marks against hours (SLOPE, marks first).
In B13 find the intercept with INTERCEPT.
In B14 predict the mark for 5.5 hours: intercept plus slope times 5.5.

checks.label: B11 is the correlation
checks.explain: Correlation runs from -1 to +1; near +1 means they rise together.

checks.label: B12 is the slope
checks.explain: The slope is the extra marks per extra hour.

checks.label: B13 is the intercept
checks.explain: The intercept is the predicted mark at zero hours.

checks.label: B14 predicts the mark at 5.5 hours
checks.explain: A prediction uses the line: intercept plus slope times the input.

activities.title: Final project: analyse a survey
activities.objective: Describe a data set, measure its spread, find a confidence interval and test a relationship.
activities.scenario: A school surveyed eight students on weekly screen time (hours, column B) and sleep (hours, column C). Report the main findings.
steps: Find the mean and median screen time (B11, B12).
Find the standard deviation of screen time (B13).
Find the standard error (B14) and a 95% margin of error (B15) for the mean screen time.
Find the correlation between screen time and sleep (B16).
Find the slope of sleep against screen time (B17).
Chart screen time by student with a bar chart.

checks.label: B11 is the mean
checks.explain: The mean describes the centre.

checks.label: B12 is the median
checks.explain: The median is the middle value.

checks.label: B13 is the standard deviation
checks.explain: The standard deviation describes the spread.

checks.label: B14 is the standard error
checks.explain: Standard error is standard deviation over the square root of n.

checks.label: B15 is the margin of error
checks.explain: Roughly 95% confidence uses 1.96 standard errors.

checks.label: B16 is the correlation
checks.explain: Correlation measures how the two move together.

checks.label: B17 is the slope of sleep on screen time
checks.explain: A negative slope means sleep falls as screen time rises.

checks.label: A bar chart of screen time
checks.hint: Chart type bar with labels A2:A9 and values B2:B9.
checks.explain: A chart shows each student's hours at a glance.
